GATE: require:[] — deliberately no hard gate; a codec/resolution gate would empty the guide given sparse body specs, and many strong hybrids are photo-first bodies with excellent video. Fit is expressed through axis weights. CRUX at 3: video_capability — codec/bit-depth/resolution/frame-rate/log + recording-limit/overheating behaviour, the defining video-body axis. SECONDARY at 2: stabilization (IBIS is what makes handheld vlogging and run-and-gun usable — the top-cited vlogging differentiator) and autofocus_body (reliable CONTINUOUS AF with face/eye tracking is what separates a video-capable body from a frustrating one; stills-grade single-AF is not enough for video). SUPPORTING at 1: evf_lcd (a vari-angle / flip-to-front screen is near-mandatory for solo vlogging and self-recording), connectivity (clean HDMI out, USB-C webcam/streaming, fast file transfer for creators), handling (long handheld takes, front-facing operation). Deliberately UNWEIGHTED (0/omitted): burst_buffer, sensor_performance, image_quality, color_rendition, build, battery_life — real, and some (battery, color/log grading) matter to video, but they are not the primary axes the corpus lets us rank video bodies on, and video_capability already absorbs codec/color-depth. gear_class excludes novelty only. DISTINCT-FINGERPRINT CHECK: unique among the body profiles by leading with video_capability 3 (every other body guide leaves it unweighted) — the video signature; distinct AF emphasis (continuous, not burst) separates it from wildlife.
